title: Air India Names Ethiopian Airlines Veteran Tewolde Gebremariam as New CEO
excerpt: The Tata-owned carrier appoints the architect of Ethiopian Airlines' rise as Africa's largest carrier to lead its turnaround following a fatal 2025 crash and record losses exceeding $2 billion.
body:
• Air India appointed former Ethiopian Airlines CEO Tewolde Gebremariam on Wednesday to lead the carrier through its most challenging period since returning to Tata Group ownership in 2022.
  • Gebremariam transformed Ethiopian Airlines into Africa's largest carrier, quadrupling revenue and nearly tripling its fleet during his decade-long tenure.
  • He succeeds Campbell Wilson, who resigned in April after a fatal 2025 crash that killed 260 people intensified pressure on the airline.
  • Air India Group posted a record loss exceeding $2 billion in fiscal 2025-26, with Tata Sons acknowledging the turnaround could take up to a decade.

Air India named former Ethiopian Airlines chief Tewolde Gebremariam as its new CEO on Wednesday, bringing in one of the aviation industry's most proven turnaround specialists to steer the loss-making carrier through a period of mounting safety scrutiny and financial pressure.

The Choice

The appointment concludes a months-long search for a chief executive during what Tata Group has acknowledged is Air India's most challenging period since the conglomerate reacquired the airline from the Indian government in 2022. Gebremariam is widely regarded as an industry heavyweight whose track record at Ethiopian Airlines established him as one of the most successful airline executives in emerging markets.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=7KsrD5pOKtI

"It takes someone with a particular set of skills and experience to navigate such a complex situation. Gebremariam is a really excellent choice to lead an airline facing multiple challenges."

— John Strickland, independent aviation analyst

During his decade leading Ethiopian Airlines, Gebremariam transformed a mid-sized regional carrier into Africa's largest airline. Revenue more than quadrupled while the fleet nearly tripled. He guided the airline through two major crises — the COVID-19 pandemic, which Ethiopian Airlines navigated without government aid, and the fatal 2019 Boeing 737 MAX crash — without ceding the carrier's growth trajectory.

After leaving Ethiopian Airlines in 2022, Gebremariam served as a senior strategic advisor at Delta Air Lines and founded TGM Advisory Services, consulting on aviation strategy and business transformation.

What He Inherits

Gebremariam succeeds Campbell Wilson, who spent four years overseeing Air India's post-privatization overhaul, including the Vistara merger, a brand refresh, and fleet modernization. Wilson resigned in April, nearly a year after a fatal crash in June 2025 that killed 260 people and triggered intensified regulatory and operational scrutiny.

Air India Group posted a record loss exceeding $2 billion in fiscal 2025-26, according to the annual report of minority shareholder Singapore Airlines, which holds roughly 25% of the carrier. Tata Sons controls the remainder.

In Air India's own annual report released last week, Tata Sons Chair N. Chandrasekaran said the airline's turnaround could take up to a decade, framing the challenge in terms that few airline executives would eagerly sign up for.

Execution Phase

"Having completed the initial phase of stabilization, integration and fleet commitments under Campbell's guidance, Air India is now entering a critical execution and expansion phase," Chandrasekaran said on Wednesday. Wilson will step down on September 30 after serving his notice period.

Analysts note that while Wilson laid important foundations — the Vistara integration consolidated Tata's airline operations, and major fleet orders for new Boeing and Airbus aircraft are in progress — the fruits of that work were just beginning to materialize when the crash forced a strategic reset.

"It's not going to be some overnight sensation that suddenly changes because there's a new boss. It will continue to take time, but Tewolde Gebremariam is better equipped than any other theoretical candidate for the role," Strickland said.

A Broader Shift

Gebremariam's appointment is part of a wider wave of airline CEO changes in 2026. IndiGo's Pieter Elbers stepped down in March, and leadership transitions have also occurred at Air Canada and several other major carriers. The churn reflects a global airline industry grappling with post-pandemic scaling, regulatory pressure, and the operational complexity of large fleet expansion programs.

For Air India, the question is whether Gebremariam's demonstrated ability to build a carrier from the ground up in a challenging market can translate to restructuring one that already has the aircraft orders, the route network, and the brand history — but needs the operational execution to match.
nri_angle: For the millions of NRIs who rely on Air India for long-haul flights between India and destinations across North America, Europe, and the Gulf, the new CEO's turnaround track record could determine whether the carrier's service, safety, and reliability finally match its expansion ambitions.
author: Diaspora Desk
